dedupe_keys.name: socio environmental geodatabase for the rio grande rio bravo basin

description: This geodatabase gathers harmonised socio-environmental GIS layers for the transboundary Rio Grande/Río Bravo basin shared by the United States and Mexico, to support integrated water resources research across the border. It covers the whole basin with 145 GIS layers grouped in five themes, including water use and hydraulic infrastructure such as dams from the US National Inventory of Dams and Mexico's CENAPRED inventory, diversions and irrigation, alongside other environmental and social layers. It was assembled by Sophie Plassin and co-authors and described in Scientific Data on 6 March 2020. The data are available for download from the Open Science Framework (doi 10.17605/OSF.IO/79426) as a single file geodatabase or as individual shapefiles and rasters, under CC BY 4.0 and free of charge; the OSF project was created in June 2019 and last modified in September 2024. Caveats: layers come from many sources with different dates and scales, compiled when the project was set up in 2019. It is useful for cross-border water infrastructure, reservoir and irrigation modelling and for climate adaptation analysis of the basin's green-blue and grey infrastructure; a related record is the Transboundary Wetlands Database.
